subject: design/local-git-codehost
statement: Run the same proposal lifecycle conformance suite against hosted and local adapters. The local suite uses real temporary bare origins under the shared-account policy. It covers the separate first configured-mainline push from the pinned init epoch, wrong/missing-epoch first-push refusal, subsequent history-gate refusal, missing-mainline draft open/prepare refusal with the first-push remedy, a configured mainline branch other than `main`, initialized-origin open, round, concurrent branch/proposal publication, stale push, prepare, readiness failure, missing receipt refusal, exact-head receipt, stale receipt refusal, proposal-head ABA (`H1→H2→H1`) with old-receipt refusal, a branch move between final read and landing push, lock, same-origin fresh-clone consistency verification after deleting the review worktree, missing or altered receipt-ref detection against the embedded bytes, reopen, abandonment, implementation proposal to a feature-integration ref, wrong-target refusal, missing/partial/stale task review aggregates, immutable aggregate-ref publication and fresh-clone recovery after the review worktree is deleted, absent/altered aggregate-ref refusal before landing and `RecordLanding`, two parallel-root task proposals on one base in each human-chosen order (second stale target refuses, reviewed rebase yields a squash child of the first landed revision, and both remain ancestors), reviewed task landing, missing/negative/stale final candidate evidence, immutable candidate-evidence-ref publication and fresh-clone recovery after the evidence worktree is deleted, absent/altered candidate-evidence-ref refusal before landing and after a landing crash, a target-main advance during final landing, distinct final proposal and feature refs, and accepted final delivery with candidate-tree and mainline-ancestry proof. It also checks that outputs disclose the unauthenticated approver, lack of independent repository identity, and absent host protection. It records every spawned command and fails if `gh`, Forgejo, or network is used.
